title: Discrepancy-Aware Graph Mask Auto-Encoder

problem.claim: Masked Graph Auto-Encoders recover masked information using node contextual information, but this approach does not generalize well to heterophilic graphs.

gap.claim: Existing methods focus on neighborhood information while ignoring discrepancy information between different nodes, resulting in indistinguishable node representations.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes a Discrepancy-Aware Graph Mask Auto-Encoder that reconstructs neighboring-node discrepancy information during masking.
The method is intended to produce more distinguishable node representations and preserve node discrepancies in low-dimensional space.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report experiments on 17 widely used benchmark datasets.
The authors report that DGMAE effectively preserves node discrepancies in low-dimensional space.
The authors report that DGMAE significantly outperforms state-of-the-art graph self-supervised learning methods on node classification, node clustering, and graph classification tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Masked Graph Auto-Encoders are described as a powerful graph self-supervised training paradigm.
Existing methods rely on node contextual information and perform poorly on heterophilic graphs because they ignore discrepancies between nodes.
The paper proposes DGMAE, which reconstructs neighboring-node discrepancy information during masking.
The authors evaluate DGMAE on 17 benchmark datasets and report preservation of discrepancies in low-dimensional space.
The authors report superiority over state-of-the-art graph self-supervised learning methods across three graph analytic tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the discrepancy definition or reconstruction objective.
The abstract does not identify the 17 datasets, baselines, metrics, or experimental conditions.
The abstract does not report numerical result values or statistical uncertainty.
